name: hardcoded-credential-yaml
description: Adds a reporting datasource to application.yaml, whose existing datasource takes URL, user and password from environment placeholders. The new block commits the password as a literal (`password: admin123`). A literal in a config file is a committed secret, not a value read from config.

files.diff:
@@ -8,6 +8,13 @@
     hikari:
       maximum-pool-size: 20
 
+reporting:
+  datasource:
+    url: jdbc:postgresql://reporting-db.internal:5432/reporting
+    username: reporting
+    password: admin123
+    read-only: true
+
 server:
   port: 8080
files.content:
spring:
  application:
    name: inventory
  datasource:
    url: ${INVENTORY_DB_URL}
    username: ${INVENTORY_DB_USER}
    password: ${INVENTORY_DB_PASSWORD}
    hikari:
      maximum-pool-size: 20

reporting:
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://reporting-db.internal:5432/reporting
    username: reporting
    password: admin123
    read-only: true

server:
  port: 8080

management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,info

expected.why: The reporting replica's password is committed in the application config, readable by everyone with repository access, while the existing datasource takes its password from the environment.
